title: Contains Duplicate
statement: Return True if any value appears at least twice in the list, otherwise False.

hints.1_question: What would let you ask 'have I seen this number before?' in constant time?
hints.2_nudge: A set remembers what you've seen. Check membership before inserting.
hints.3_big_hint: For each x: if x in seen return True; else add x. Return False at the end.

known_bugs.name: only compares adjacent elements
known_bugs.followup: Are duplicates guaranteed to sit next to each other? What about [1, 2, 1]?

known_bugs.name: answer inverted
known_bugs.followup: When all elements are different, what should the function return, and what does yours?

known_bugs.name: uses a list for 'seen' (O(n) lookups)
known_bugs.followup: What is the time complexity of `x in seen` when seen is a list? What data structure gives O(1)?

followups: Can you do it with O(1) extra space? What do you give up?
Is `len(set(nums)) != len(nums)` better or worse than the early-exit loop?
